material_id:
Hari ketujuh: kita belajar membaca **seragam** kata, yaitu akhirannya. Dari akhiran, kita tahu sebuah kata bekerja sebagai benda, sifat, keterangan, atau kerja. Di Listening kita mencatat angka dan urutan dalam kuliah, dan di Reading kita menaklukkan soal NOT/EXCEPT.

=== listening
## Mencatat lecture: topik, angka, urutan
Dosen sering memberi **penanda urutan**: *First, Second, And third, Finally, After that, Later*. Dosen juga menyebut **angka**: tahun, jumlah, persentase. Catat dengan singkat: angka + kata kerja (*1840 jual*, *2x lipat*). Soal Part C hampir selalu menanyakan salah satunya.
Perumpamaan: mencatat lecture itu seperti menulis daftar belanja saat mendengar resep di radio. Kamu tidak menyalin semua kalimat, cukup bahan, jumlah, dan urutannya.
> First/Second/Finally → nomori catatan · tahun/jumlah → tulis angka + kata kerja
✓ Dengar topik di kalimat pembuka (*Today we're going to talk about…*)
✓ Pasangkan setiap angka dengan kejadiannya
✓ Soal NOT di lecture: centang yang disebut, sisakan yang tidak
✕ Menukar dua angka yang mirip (1843 vs 1847)
✕ Memilih jawaban karena kata yang sama tetapi kejadiannya berbeda

=== structure
## Word form: akhiran menentukan kelas kata
[[suffix]] (akhiran) adalah seragam kata. Akhiran **noun**: *-tion, -ment, -ness, -ity, -ance/-ence, -ery*. Akhiran **adjective**: *-ous, -ive, -ful, -al, -ic, -ent/-ant*. Akhiran **adverb**: biasanya *-ly*. Akhiran **verb**: *-ize, -en, -ify*. Lihat posisinya: setelah *the/a/his* butuh noun; sebelum noun butuh adjective; menerangkan verb butuh adverb.
Perumpamaan: akhiran itu seperti seragam kerja. Dari seragamnya kamu tahu dia satpam, perawat, atau koki. Kalau seragamnya salah, ia salah tempat.
> the/a/his + ___ → noun · ___ + noun → adjective · verb + ___ → adverb
✓ an important **discovery** · a **significant** effect · spoke **enthusiastically**
✓ The **construction** took two years.
✓ physical and mental **health**
✕ a **clearly** explanation (sebelum noun butuh adjective)
✕ The **govern** announced… (setelah *The* butuh noun)

=== reading
## Soal NOT / EXCEPT
Soal *All of the following … EXCEPT* atau *Which is NOT mentioned* meminta satu pilihan yang **tidak** sesuai teks. Strategi: temukan bagian teks yang dimaksud, lalu **centang** setiap pilihan yang memang tertulis. Pilihan yang tersisa adalah jawabannya. Waspadai pilihan yang memakai kata dari teks tetapi membalik maknanya.
Perumpamaan: soal EXCEPT itu seperti absen kelas. Panggil satu per satu; yang tidak menjawab "hadir" itulah jawabannya.
> Cari bagian teks → centang 3 pilihan yang ada → sisakan 1
✓ Baca soal dua kali: apakah yang dicari yang BENAR atau yang TIDAK?
✓ Cek angka dan waktu dengan teliti (sebelum 1500 vs awal abad 17)
✕ Memilih pilihan pertama yang terlihat benar (lupa kata NOT)
✕ Mencentang pilihan hanya karena ada satu kata yang sama
material_en:
Day seven: we learn to read a word's **uniform**, its ending. The ending tells you whether a word works as a noun, adjective, adverb, or verb. In Listening we note numbers and sequence in lectures, and in Reading we conquer NOT/EXCEPT questions.

=== listening
## Lecture notes: topic, numbers, sequence
Lecturers often give **sequence markers**: *First, Second, And third, Finally, After that, Later*. They also give **numbers**: years, amounts, percentages. Note them briefly: number + verb (*1840 on sale*, *2x*). Part C questions almost always ask about one of them.
Analogy: taking lecture notes is like writing a shopping list while hearing a recipe on the radio. You don't copy every sentence, just the ingredients, amounts, and order.
> First/Second/Finally → number your notes · years/amounts → write number + verb
✓ Hear the topic in the opening line (*Today we're going to talk about…*)
✓ Pair each number with its event
✓ NOT questions in lectures: tick what was said, keep what wasn't
✕ Swapping two similar numbers (1843 vs 1847)
✕ Choosing an answer for a shared word when the event is different

=== structure
## Word form: the ending decides the job
A [[suffix]] is a word's uniform. **Noun** endings: *-tion, -ment, -ness, -ity, -ance/-ence, -ery*. **Adjective** endings: *-ous, -ive, -ful, -al, -ic, -ent/-ant*. **Adverb** endings: usually *-ly*. **Verb** endings: *-ize, -en, -ify*. Then check the slot: after *the/a/his* you need a noun; before a noun, an adjective; describing a verb, an adverb.
Analogy: an ending is a work uniform. From the uniform you know who's the guard, the nurse, or the cook. In the wrong uniform, they're in the wrong place.
> the/a/his + ___ → noun · ___ + noun → adjective · verb + ___ → adverb
✓ an important **discovery** · a **significant** effect · spoke **enthusiastically**
✓ The **construction** took two years.
✓ physical and mental **health**
✕ a **clearly** explanation (before a noun you need an adjective)
✕ The **govern** announced… (after *The* you need a noun)

=== reading
## NOT / EXCEPT questions
*All of the following … EXCEPT* or *Which is NOT mentioned* asks for the one option that does **not** match the text. Strategy: find the relevant part, then **tick** each option that really is written there. The one left over is the answer. Watch for options that reuse the text's words but reverse their meaning.
Analogy: an EXCEPT question is a roll call. Call each name; the one who doesn't answer "present" is your answer.
> Find the passage part → tick the 3 that appear → keep the 1 left
✓ Read the question twice: are you looking for what IS true or what is NOT?
✓ Check numbers and dates carefully (before 1500 vs the early 1600s)
✕ Picking the first option that looks true (forgetting the NOT)
✕ Ticking an option just because one word matches

script.speaker: W1
script.text: How many pages does the history report need to be?

script.speaker: M2
script.text: At least ten, but Professor Kim said no more than fifteen.

questions.prompt: What does the man say about the report?
options: It must be exactly ten pages.
It should be between ten and fifteen pages.
It is due in fifteen days.
It can be as long as the students want.
questions.key_sentence: At least ten, but Professor Kim said no more than fifteen.
questions.key_translation_id: Minimal sepuluh, tapi Profesor Kim bilang tidak boleh lebih dari lima belas.
questions.why_correct_id: Langkah 1: 'At least ten' = minimal sepuluh halaman. Langkah 2: 'no more than fifteen' = maksimal lima belas halaman. Jadi panjang laporan harus di antara sepuluh dan lima belas halaman.
questions.why_correct_en: Step 1: 'At least ten' = a minimum of ten pages. Step 2: 'no more than fifteen' = a maximum of fifteen. So the report should be between ten and fifteen pages.

why_wrong_id.0: 'At least ten' berarti boleh lebih dari sepuluh, bukan tepat sepuluh.
why_wrong_id.2: 'Fifteen' adalah batas halaman, bukan jumlah hari sampai tenggat.
why_wrong_id.3: Ada batas atas: tidak lebih dari lima belas.

why_wrong_en.0: 'At least ten' allows more than ten, not exactly ten.
why_wrong_en.2: 'Fifteen' is the page limit, not days until the deadline.
why_wrong_en.3: There's an upper limit: no more than fifteen.

questions.analogy_id: 'At least' dan 'no more than' itu seperti pagar di dua sisi jalan: kamu boleh berjalan di mana saja di antara keduanya.
questions.analogy_en: 'At least' and 'no more than' are fences on both sides of a road: you can walk anywhere between them.
questions.tip_id: at least = minimal · no more than / at most = maksimal. Gabungkan keduanya menjadi rentang.
questions.tip_en: at least = minimum · no more than / at most = maximum. Combine them into a range.

script.speaker: W2
script.text: It closed at six, but the one in the student center stays open until nine.

questions.prompt: What does the woman imply?
options: The man can still buy books at another store.
The man should come back tomorrow at six.
The student center closed at six.
questions.key_sentence: It closed at six, but the one in the student center stays open until nine.
questions.key_translation_id: Toko itu tutup jam enam, tapi yang di gedung kemahasiswaan buka sampai jam sembilan.
questions.why_correct_id: Langkah 1: toko yang ditanyakan sudah tutup jam enam. Langkah 2: 'but the one in the student center stays open until nine' = ada toko lain yang masih buka. Jadi pria masih bisa membeli buku di toko lain itu.
questions.why_correct_en: Step 1: the bookstore he asked about closed at six. Step 2: 'but the one in the student center stays open until nine' = another store is still open. So he can still buy books there.

why_wrong_id.1: Ia tidak menyuruh datang besok; ia menunjukkan toko lain yang masih buka.
why_wrong_id.2: Yang tutup jam enam adalah toko pertama; toko di gedung kemahasiswaan buka sampai jam sembilan.
why_wrong_id.3: Kebalikannya: satu toko masih buka.

why_wrong_en.1: She doesn't suggest tomorrow; she points to another open store.
why_wrong_en.2: The first store closed at six; the student center one is open until nine.
why_wrong_en.3: The opposite: one store is still open.

questions.analogy_id: Kata 'the one' itu seperti menunjuk ke kembaran: toko yang lain dengan fungsi yang sama.
questions.analogy_en: 'The one' is like pointing to a twin: another store doing the same job.
questions.tip_id: Dua jam berbeda di satu kalimat → pasangkan setiap jam dengan tempatnya.
questions.tip_en: Two times in one sentence → pair each time with its place.

script.speaker: W1
script.text: I'm thinking of taking the eight a.m. statistics section.

script.speaker: M1
script.text: Are you sure? You've been late to every morning class this semester.

questions.prompt: What does the man imply?
options: Statistics is too difficult for her.
He has already taken the course.
The eight a.m. section is full.
She may have trouble attending an early class.
questions.key_sentence: Are you sure? You've been late to every morning class this semester.
questions.key_translation_id: Yakin? Semester ini kamu terlambat di setiap kelas pagi.
questions.why_correct_id: Langkah 1: 'Are you sure?' menunjukkan keraguan. Langkah 2: alasannya, wanita selalu terlambat di setiap kelas pagi. Langkah 3: jadi pria menyiratkan bahwa kelas jam delapan pagi bisa menyulitkan wanita.
questions.why_correct_en: Step 1: 'Are you sure?' shows doubt. Step 2: the reason: she's been late to every morning class. Step 3: so he implies an 8 a.m. class may be a problem for her.

why_wrong_id.0: Tingkat kesulitan statistika tidak dibahas; yang dibahas jamnya.
why_wrong_id.1: Tidak ada informasi bahwa pria pernah mengambil kelas itu.
why_wrong_id.2: Kuota kelas tidak disebut.

why_wrong_en.0: The subject's difficulty isn't discussed; the time is.
why_wrong_en.1: Nothing says he took the course.
why_wrong_en.2: Class capacity isn't mentioned.

questions.analogy_id: 'Are you sure?' + bukti masa lalu itu seperti teman yang mengingatkan rekor burukmu sebelum kamu membuat janji baru.
questions.analogy_en: 'Are you sure?' + past evidence is a friend reminding you of your track record before you make a new promise.
questions.tip_id: Pertanyaan balik (Are you sure? Really?) + fakta = keraguan. Cari pilihan tentang masalah yang mungkin muncul.
questions.tip_en: A question back (Are you sure? Really?) + a fact = doubt. Look for the option about a likely problem.

script.speaker: M2
script.text: Did you finish the lab report, or are you still working on the graphs?

script.speaker: W2
script.text: The graphs are done. It's the conclusion I'm stuck on.

questions.prompt: What does the woman mean?
options: She has not started the report.
She needs help making the graphs.
She is having trouble writing the conclusion.
She has finished the whole report.
questions.key_sentence: It's the conclusion I'm stuck on.
questions.why_correct_id: Langkah 1: 'The graphs are done' = grafiknya sudah selesai. Langkah 2: 'It's the conclusion I'm stuck on' = ia buntu di bagian kesimpulan. Jadi ia kesulitan menulis kesimpulan.
questions.why_correct_en: Step 1: 'The graphs are done' = the graphs are finished. Step 2: 'It's the conclusion I'm stuck on' = she's stuck on the conclusion. So she's having trouble writing it.

why_wrong_id.0: Grafiknya sudah selesai, jadi laporannya sudah dimulai.
why_wrong_id.1: Grafik sudah selesai; ia tidak butuh bantuan di sana.
why_wrong_id.3: Kesimpulannya belum selesai, jadi laporan belum rampung.

why_wrong_en.0: The graphs are done, so she has started.
why_wrong_en.1: The graphs are finished; she doesn't need help there.
why_wrong_en.3: The conclusion isn't done, so the report isn't finished.

questions.analogy_id: 'Stuck on' itu seperti mobil yang tersangkut lumpur: sudah jalan jauh, tapi berhenti di satu titik.
questions.analogy_en: 'Stuck on' is a car caught in mud: it got far, but it's stopped at one point.
questions.tip_id: Pola 'It's X that…' menekankan X. Jawaban hampir selalu tentang X.
questions.tip_en: 'It's X that…' stresses X. The answer is almost always about X.

script.speaker: W1
script.text: Did you see the email about the new recycling program in the dorms?

script.speaker: M2
script.text: I did. Starting next Monday, each floor gets three bins: blue for paper, green for glass, and yellow for plastic and cans.

script.speaker: W1
script.text: What about food waste? That's what fills up our trash the most.

script.speaker: M2
script.text: That's the second phase. They'll add compost bins in the kitchens in March, after they see how the first phase goes.

script.speaker: W1
script.text: Makes sense. Do we have to wash the containers before we recycle them?

script.speaker: M2
script.text: Just rinse them. The email said dirty containers can ruin a whole bag of recycling.

script.speaker: W1
script.text: Good to know. I'll put a sign on our kitchen door so everyone remembers the colors.

script.speaker: M2
script.text: Great idea. Maybe add a note about rinsing, too.

questions.prompt: What are the speakers mainly discussing?
options: A new recycling system in their dormitory
A cleaning schedule for the kitchen
A broken trash bin on their floor
questions.key_sentence: Did you see the email about the new recycling program in the dorms?
questions.key_translation_id: Kamu sudah lihat email tentang program daur ulang baru di asrama?
questions.why_correct_id: Langkah 1: kalimat pembuka menyebut topik: program daur ulang baru di asrama. Langkah 2: seluruh percakapan membahas aturannya: warna tempat sampah, tahap kedua untuk sisa makanan, dan cara membilas wadah.
questions.why_correct_en: Step 1: the opening line names the topic: the new recycling program in the dorms. Step 2: the whole talk covers its rules: bin colours, the food-waste phase, and rinsing containers.

why_wrong_id.1: Dapur disebut sebagai tempat tempat kompos dan tanda, bukan jadwal bersih-bersih.
why_wrong_id.2: Tidak ada tempat sampah yang rusak.
why_wrong_id.3: Email itu tentang program daur ulang; tidak disebut bahwa email itu dari dosen.

why_wrong_en.1: The kitchen is where compost bins and a sign go, not a cleaning schedule.
why_wrong_en.2: No bin is broken.
why_wrong_en.3: The email is about the program; nothing says it's from a professor.

questions.analogy_id: Kalimat pembuka itu seperti judul berita: 'program daur ulang baru di asrama'. Sisanya adalah isi beritanya.
questions.analogy_en: The opening line is the news headline: 'new recycling program in the dorms'. The rest is the story.
questions.tip_id: Untuk soal topik, pilih jawaban yang mencakup seluruh percakapan, bukan satu detail (email, dapur).
questions.tip_en: For topic questions, pick the answer that covers the whole talk, not one detail (email, kitchen).

questions.prompt: Which bin should be used for glass?
questions.key_sentence: blue for paper, green for glass, and yellow for plastic and cans.
questions.key_translation_id: biru untuk kertas, hijau untuk kaca, dan kuning untuk plastik dan kaleng.
questions.why_correct_id: Langkah 1: pria menyebut tiga tempat sampah dengan warnanya. Langkah 2: urutannya: biru untuk kertas, HIJAU untuk kaca, kuning untuk plastik dan kaleng. Jadi kaca masuk tempat sampah hijau.
questions.why_correct_en: Step 1: the man lists three bins and their colours. Step 2: blue for paper, GREEN for glass, yellow for plastic and cans. So glass goes in the green bin.

why_wrong_id.0: Biru untuk kertas.
why_wrong_id.2: Kuning untuk plastik dan kaleng.
why_wrong_id.3: Tempat kompos untuk sisa makanan, dan baru datang bulan Maret.

why_wrong_en.0: Blue is for paper.
why_wrong_en.2: Yellow is for plastic and cans.
why_wrong_en.3: Compost bins are for food waste and only arrive in March.

questions.analogy_id: Daftar warna seperti ini itu seperti kode loker: catat pasangan warna dan isinya, jangan hanya warnanya.
questions.analogy_en: A colour list like this is a locker code: write down each colour with its contents, not just the colours.
questions.tip_id: Saat mendengar daftar (X for A, Y for B), tulis pasangannya dengan singkat: biru-kertas, hijau-kaca.
questions.tip_en: When you hear a list (X for A, Y for B), jot the pairs: blue-paper, green-glass.

questions.prompt: When will compost bins be added?
options: At the end of the year
questions.key_sentence: They'll add compost bins in the kitchens in March, after they see how the first phase goes.
questions.key_translation_id: Mereka akan menambah tempat kompos di dapur pada bulan Maret, setelah melihat hasil tahap pertama.
questions.why_correct_id: Langkah 1: tempat kompos disebut sebagai 'the second phase' (tahap kedua). Langkah 2: waktunya disebut jelas: 'in March', setelah melihat hasil tahap pertama.
questions.why_correct_en: Step 1: compost bins are 'the second phase'. Step 2: the timing is stated: 'in March', after seeing how the first phase goes.

why_wrong_id.0: 'Next Monday' adalah waktu mulainya tahap pertama (tiga tempat sampah), bukan tempat kompos.
why_wrong_id.1: Tidak disebut bahwa tempat kompos menunggu permintaan mahasiswa.
why_wrong_id.3: Akhir tahun tidak disebut.

why_wrong_en.0: 'Next Monday' is when the first phase (three bins) starts, not the compost bins.
why_wrong_en.1: Nothing says compost bins depend on student requests.
why_wrong_en.3: The end of the year isn't mentioned.

questions.analogy_id: Dua tahap dengan dua waktu itu seperti dua halte bus: Senin depan untuk tahap pertama, Maret untuk tahap kedua.
questions.analogy_en: Two phases with two dates are like two bus stops: next Monday for phase one, March for phase two.
questions.tip_id: Percakapan dengan beberapa waktu (next Monday, March) → cocokkan setiap waktu dengan kegiatannya.
questions.tip_en: With several times in a talk (next Monday, March), match each time to its activity.

script.speaker: LEC
script.text: Today we're going to talk about a small object that changed communication: the postage stamp. Before 1840, sending a letter in Britain was complicated and expensive. The cost depended on the distance and on the number of sheets of paper, and it was usually the person who received the letter, not the sender, who paid. Many people simply refused to accept letters, so the post office often delivered mail and received nothing. In 1837, a teacher named Rowland Hill proposed a simple solution. First, the price should be the same for any distance within the country. Second, the sender should pay in advance. And third, payment would be shown with a small printed label that could be stuck onto the envelope. Parliament accepted the plan, and in May 1840 the world's first adhesive stamp, called the Penny Black, went on sale. The results were dramatic. The number of letters sent in Britain more than doubled within a year. Other countries soon followed. Brazil introduced stamps in 1843, and the United States issued its first national stamps in 1847.

questions.prompt: What is the lecture mainly about?
options: Why letters were expensive to write
The life of a famous British teacher
How the first postage stamp changed the mail system
questions.key_sentence: Today we're going to talk about a small object that changed communication: the postage stamp.
questions.key_translation_id: Hari ini kita akan membahas benda kecil yang mengubah komunikasi: perangko.
questions.why_correct_id: Langkah 1: kalimat pembuka menyebut topik: perangko, benda kecil yang mengubah komunikasi. Langkah 2: isi kuliah: masalah pos sebelum 1840, usulan Rowland Hill, perangko pertama, dan dampaknya.
questions.why_correct_en: Step 1: the opening line names the topic: the postage stamp, a small object that changed communication. Step 2: the lecture covers the problem before 1840, Hill's proposal, the first stamp, and its impact.

why_wrong_id.0: Biaya MENGIRIM surat yang mahal, bukan menulisnya; itu pun hanya latar belakang.
why_wrong_id.1: Rowland Hill disebut karena usulannya, bukan kisah hidupnya.
why_wrong_id.3: Cara mencetak perangko masa kini tidak dibahas.

why_wrong_en.0: Sending, not writing, was expensive, and that's only background.
why_wrong_en.1: Rowland Hill appears for his proposal, not his life story.
why_wrong_en.3: Modern printing isn't discussed.

questions.analogy_id: Topik kuliah itu seperti nama mata pelajaran di jadwal: disebut di awal, lalu semua isi kelas menjelaskannya.
questions.analogy_en: A lecture's topic is like the subject name on a timetable: stated at the start, then the whole class explains it.
questions.tip_id: Pilihan topik yang hanya membahas latar belakang (mengapa mahal) biasanya terlalu sempit.
questions.tip_en: A topic option about background alone (why it was expensive) is usually too narrow.

questions.prompt: Which of the following was NOT part of Rowland Hill's proposal?
options: A single price for any distance
Payment by the sender in advance
A printed label stuck on the envelope
A higher price for letters with more pages
questions.key_sentence: First, the price should be the same for any distance within the country.
questions.key_translation_id: Pertama, harganya harus sama untuk jarak berapa pun di dalam negeri.
questions.why_correct_id: Langkah 1: dosen menyebut tiga bagian usulan dengan penanda urutan: First (harga sama untuk jarak berapa pun), Second (pengirim membayar di muka), And third (label cetak yang ditempel). Langkah 2: harga berdasarkan jumlah halaman justru sistem LAMA sebelum 1840, bukan usulan Hill.
questions.why_correct_en: Step 1: the lecturer lists three parts with sequence markers: First (same price for any distance), Second (sender pays in advance), And third (a printed label stuck on). Step 2: pricing by number of pages was the OLD system before 1840, not Hill's idea.

why_wrong_id.0: Disebut sebagai bagian pertama ('First').
why_wrong_id.1: Disebut sebagai bagian kedua ('Second').
why_wrong_id.2: Disebut sebagai bagian ketiga ('And third').

why_wrong_en.0: It's the first part ('First').
why_wrong_en.1: It's the second part ('Second').
why_wrong_en.2: It's the third part ('And third').

questions.analogy_id: Penanda First, Second, And third itu seperti nomor rak: tiga rak terisi, dan pilihan keempat tidak punya rak di usulan Hill.
questions.analogy_en: First, Second, And third are shelf numbers: three shelves are filled, and the fourth option has no shelf in Hill's plan.
questions.tip_id: Saat dosen berkata 'First… Second… Third…', nomori catatanmu. Soal NOT sering menguji daftar ini.
questions.tip_en: When a lecturer says 'First… Second… Third…', number your notes. NOT questions often test such lists.

questions.prompt: What happened to the number of letters sent in Britain after stamps were introduced?
options: It more than doubled within a year.
questions.key_sentence: The number of letters sent in Britain more than doubled within a year.
questions.key_translation_id: Jumlah surat yang dikirim di Inggris naik lebih dari dua kali lipat dalam setahun.
questions.why_correct_id: Langkah 1: setelah 'The results were dramatic', dosen menyebut hasilnya. Langkah 2: jumlah surat 'more than doubled within a year' (naik lebih dari dua kali lipat dalam setahun).
questions.why_correct_en: Step 1: after 'The results were dramatic', the lecturer gives the result. Step 2: the number of letters 'more than doubled within a year'.

why_wrong_id.0: Kebalikannya: jumlah surat naik, bukan turun.
why_wrong_id.2: 1843 adalah tahun Brasil memperkenalkan perangko, bukan tahun perubahan di Inggris.
why_wrong_id.3: Kuliah hanya menyebut naik lebih dari dua kali lipat dalam SETAHUN, bukan setiap tahun sampai 1847.

why_wrong_en.0: The opposite: letters increased, not decreased.
why_wrong_en.2: 1843 is when Brazil introduced stamps, not a change in Britain.
why_wrong_en.3: It more than doubled within ONE year, not every year until 1847.

questions.analogy_id: 'The results were dramatic' itu seperti drum sebelum pengumuman juara: angka penting akan segera disebut.
questions.analogy_en: 'The results were dramatic' is a drumroll before the winner: an important number is coming.
questions.tip_id: Kata 'dramatic, surprising, remarkable' sering mendahului angka yang ditanyakan.
questions.tip_en: 'Dramatic, surprising, remarkable' often come right before the number being tested.

items.prompt: The scientists made an important ______ about the origin of the disease.
items.why_correct_id: Langkah 1: setelah 'an important' (article + adjective) dibutuhkan noun (kata benda). Langkah 2: akhiran *-y* pada 'discovery' menandai noun. Jawabannya **discovery**.
items.why_correct_en: Step 1: after 'an important' (article + adjective) you need a noun. Step 2: 'discovery' is the noun form. The answer is **discovery**.

why_wrong_id.1: 'discover' adalah verb (kata kerja); tidak bisa setelah 'an important'.
why_wrong_id.2: 'discovered' adalah V2/V3, bukan noun.
why_wrong_id.3: 'discovering' (V-ing) tidak tepat di sini; 'make a discovery' adalah kolokasi tetap.

why_wrong_en.1: 'discover' is a verb; it can't follow 'an important'.
why_wrong_en.2: 'discovered' is V2/V3, not a noun.
why_wrong_en.3: 'discovering' doesn't fit; 'make a discovery' is a fixed collocation.

items.analogy_id: Article + adjective itu seperti kursi penumpang yang sudah disiapkan: yang duduk harus noun.
items.analogy_en: Article + adjective is a seat already set out: only a noun can sit there.

items.prompt: The museum guide spoke ______ about the history of the paintings.
items.why_correct_id: Langkah 1: kata yang hilang menerangkan cara pemandu berbicara, yaitu menerangkan verb (kata kerja) 'spoke'. Langkah 2: yang menerangkan verb adalah [[adverb]] (kata keterangan), biasanya berakhiran *-ly*: **enthusiastically**.
items.why_correct_en: Step 1: the missing word describes how the guide spoke, so it modifies the verb 'spoke'. Step 2: verbs are modified by adverbs, usually ending in -ly: **enthusiastically**.

why_wrong_id.0: 'enthusiasm' adalah noun (semangat), tidak bisa menerangkan verb secara langsung.
why_wrong_id.1: 'enthusiastic' adalah adjective (kata sifat); adjective menerangkan noun, bukan verb.
why_wrong_id.2: 'enthusiast' adalah noun untuk orang (penggemar).

why_wrong_en.0: 'enthusiasm' is a noun; it can't directly modify a verb.
why_wrong_en.1: 'enthusiastic' is an adjective; adjectives describe nouns, not verbs.
why_wrong_en.2: 'enthusiast' is a noun for a person (a fan).

items.analogy_id: Adverb itu gaya menyetir: menerangkan BAGAIMANA mesin (spoke) bekerja.
items.analogy_en: An adverb is driving style: it tells HOW the engine (spoke) runs.
items.tip_id: Kata kerja aksi + ___ yang menjawab 'bagaimana?' → pilih bentuk -ly.
items.tip_en: Action verb + ___ answering 'how?' → choose the -ly form.

items.prompt: The new policy had a ______ effect on student attendance.
items.why_correct_id: Langkah 1: rumpang berada di antara 'a' dan noun (kata benda) 'effect'. Langkah 2: posisi sebelum noun diisi [[adjective]] (kata sifat). Akhiran *-ant* menandai adjective: **significant**.
items.why_correct_en: Step 1: the blank sits between 'a' and the noun 'effect'. Step 2: the slot before a noun takes an adjective. The -ant ending marks one: **significant**.

why_wrong_id.0: 'signify' adalah verb (kata kerja).
why_wrong_id.1: 'significance' adalah noun; dua noun berjejer ('a significance effect') tidak tepat di sini.
why_wrong_id.3: 'significantly' adalah adverb; adverb tidak menerangkan noun.

why_wrong_en.0: 'signify' is a verb.
why_wrong_en.1: 'significance' is a noun; 'a significance effect' doesn't work here.
why_wrong_en.3: 'significantly' is an adverb; adverbs don't describe nouns.

items.analogy_id: Adjective itu cat mobil: dioleskan langsung ke benda (effect).
items.analogy_en: An adjective is the paint: applied directly to the thing (effect).
items.tip_id: a/an + ___ + noun → adjective. Hafalkan akhiran adjective: -ant/-ent, -ous, -ive, -ful, -al.
items.tip_en: a/an + ___ + noun → adjective. Learn adjective endings: -ant/-ent, -ous, -ive, -ful, -al.

items.prompt: Many students find it ______ to study in a quiet library than at home.
items.why_correct_id: Langkah 1: pola 'find it + ___ + to …' butuh [[adjective]] (kata sifat) setelah 'it': find it easy, find it difficult. Langkah 2: ada 'than', jadi butuh bentuk perbandingan. Langkah 3: adjective + perbandingan = **more productive**.
items.why_correct_en: Step 1: 'find it + ___ + to …' needs an adjective after 'it' (find it easy, find it difficult). Step 2: 'than' calls for a comparative. Step 3: so the answer is **more productive**.

why_wrong_id.0: 'more productively' adalah adverb; setelah 'find it' dibutuhkan adjective.
why_wrong_id.2: 'productivity' adalah noun dan tidak bisa dibandingkan dengan 'than' dalam pola ini.
why_wrong_id.3: 'most produce' memakai verb dan superlative; keduanya tidak cocok dengan 'than'.

why_wrong_en.0: 'more productively' is an adverb; 'find it' needs an adjective.
why_wrong_en.2: 'productivity' is a noun and doesn't fit this 'than' comparison.
why_wrong_en.3: 'most produce' uses a verb and a superlative; neither fits 'than'.

items.analogy_id: 'Find it ___' itu seperti memberi nilai pada sesuatu: nilainya adalah sifat (productive), bukan cara (productively).
items.analogy_en: 'Find it ___' gives something a rating: the rating is a quality (productive), not a manner (productively).
items.tip_id: find/make/consider + it + ADJECTIVE + to V1. Jangan tertipu bentuk -ly.
items.tip_en: find/make/consider + it + ADJECTIVE + to V1. Don't be fooled by -ly forms.

items.prompt: The {A}manager{/A} gave a {B}clearly{/B} {C}explanation{/C} of the new {D}rules{/D}.
items.why_correct_id: Langkah 1: 'clearly' berada di antara 'a' dan noun (kata benda) 'explanation'. Langkah 2: posisi sebelum noun butuh [[adjective]] (kata sifat), bukan adverb. Jadi 'clearly' harus menjadi **clear**.
items.why_correct_en: Step 1: 'clearly' sits between 'a' and the noun 'explanation'. Step 2: before a noun you need an adjective, not an adverb. So 'clearly' should be **clear**.

why_wrong_id.0: 'manager' adalah noun yang tepat sebagai subject.
why_wrong_id.2: 'explanation' adalah noun yang tepat setelah adjective.
why_wrong_id.3: 'the new rules' adalah frasa benda yang benar.

why_wrong_en.0: 'manager' is a correct noun subject.
why_wrong_en.2: 'explanation' is a correct noun after the adjective.
why_wrong_en.3: 'the new rules' is a correct noun phrase.

items.analogy_id: Adverb di depan noun itu seperti stiker gaya menyetir yang ditempel di cat mobil: salah tempat.
items.analogy_en: An adverb before a noun is a driving-style sticker stuck on the paint job: wrong place.
items.tip_id: a/an + ___ + noun: kalau ada -ly di posisi itu, hampir pasti salah.
items.tip_en: a/an + ___ + noun: an -ly word in that slot is almost always wrong.

items.why_correct_id: Langkah 1: setelah 'The' dan sebagai subject (pelaku) kalimat, dibutuhkan noun (kata benda). Langkah 2: 'govern' adalah verb (kata kerja). Bentuk noun-nya **government** (akhiran *-ment*).
items.why_correct_en: Step 1: after 'The', as the subject, you need a noun. Step 2: 'govern' is a verb. The noun is **government** (-ment ending).

why_wrong_id.1: 'measures' (langkah-langkah) adalah noun jamak yang benar.
why_wrong_id.2: 'to reduce' adalah infinitive (to + kata kerja dasar) yang benar.
why_wrong_id.3: 'air pollution' adalah frasa benda yang benar.

why_wrong_en.1: 'measures' is a correct plural noun.
why_wrong_en.2: 'to reduce' is a correct infinitive.
why_wrong_en.3: 'air pollution' is a correct noun phrase.

items.analogy_id: Kursi sopir hanya untuk noun. 'Govern' masih berseragam verb, jadi harus ganti seragam menjadi 'government'.
items.analogy_en: The driver's seat is for nouns only. 'Govern' is still in a verb uniform; it must change into 'government'.
items.tip_id: The + ___ + verb → ___ harus noun. Cek akhiran -ment, -tion, -ity.
items.tip_en: The + ___ + verb → ___ must be a noun. Check for -ment, -tion, -ity.

items.prompt: Regular exercise {A}improves{/A} both physical and mental {B}healthy{/B} and {C}reduces{/C} {D}stress{/D}.
items.why_correct_id: Langkah 1: 'improves both physical and mental ___' butuh object berupa noun (kata benda); 'physical' dan 'mental' adalah adjective yang menerangkannya. Langkah 2: 'healthy' adalah adjective. Noun-nya **health**.
items.why_correct_en: Step 1: 'improves both physical and mental ___' needs a noun object; 'physical' and 'mental' are adjectives describing it. Step 2: 'healthy' is an adjective. The noun is **health**.

why_wrong_id.0: 'improves' tunggal, cocok dengan 'Regular exercise'.
why_wrong_id.2: 'reduces' sejajar dengan 'improves'. Benar.
why_wrong_id.3: 'stress' adalah noun yang tepat sebagai object 'reduces'.

why_wrong_en.0: 'improves' is singular, matching 'Regular exercise'.
why_wrong_en.2: 'reduces' is parallel with 'improves'. Correct.
why_wrong_en.3: 'stress' is a correct noun object of 'reduces'.

items.analogy_id: Dua adjective (physical, mental) itu cat. Cat butuh benda untuk dioles: health, bukan healthy.
items.analogy_en: Two adjectives (physical, mental) are paint. Paint needs a thing to cover: health, not healthy.
items.tip_id: Adjective + ___ di akhir frasa → ___ harus noun.
items.tip_en: Adjective + ___ at the end of a phrase → ___ must be a noun.

items.prompt: The {A}construct{/A} of the new library {B}took{/B} nearly two years because of {C}frequent{/C} {D}delays{/D}.
items.why_correct_id: Langkah 1: 'The ___ of the new library' adalah subject (pelaku), jadi butuh noun (kata benda). Langkah 2: 'construct' adalah verb. Noun-nya **construction** (akhiran *-tion*).
items.why_correct_en: Step 1: 'The ___ of the new library' is the subject, so it needs a noun. Step 2: 'construct' is a verb. The noun is **construction** (-tion ending).

why_wrong_id.1: 'took' adalah V2 dari 'take', cocok untuk kejadian lampau.
why_wrong_id.2: 'frequent' adalah adjective yang menerangkan 'delays'.
why_wrong_id.3: 'delays' adalah noun jamak yang benar setelah 'because of'.

why_wrong_en.1: 'took' is the V2 of 'take', fitting a past event.
why_wrong_en.2: 'frequent' is an adjective describing 'delays'.
why_wrong_en.3: 'delays' is a correct plural noun after 'because of'.

items.analogy_id: Pola 'The ___ of …' itu seperti bingkai foto yang hanya muat benda, bukan aksi.
items.analogy_en: 'The ___ of …' is a picture frame that fits only a thing, not an action.
items.tip_id: The + ___ + of → noun. Ubah verb menjadi -tion/-ment/-ance.
items.tip_en: The + ___ + of → noun. Turn the verb into -tion/-ment/-ance.

items.prompt: The village is {A}famous{/A} for its {B}traditional{/B} music and {C}colorful{/C} {D}decorate{/D}.
items.why_correct_id: Langkah 1: 'its traditional music and colorful ___' menyejajarkan dua frasa benda. Langkah 2: setelah adjective (kata sifat) 'colorful' butuh noun (kata benda). 'decorate' adalah verb; noun-nya **decorations**.
items.why_correct_en: Step 1: 'its traditional music and colorful ___' pairs two noun phrases. Step 2: after the adjective 'colorful' you need a noun. 'decorate' is a verb; the noun is **decorations**.

why_wrong_id.0: 'famous for' adalah pola adjective + preposition yang benar.
why_wrong_id.1: 'traditional' adalah adjective yang menerangkan 'music'.
why_wrong_id.2: 'colorful' adalah adjective yang tepat sebelum noun.

why_wrong_en.0: 'famous for' is a correct adjective + preposition pattern.
why_wrong_en.1: 'traditional' is an adjective describing 'music'.
why_wrong_en.2: 'colorful' is a correct adjective before a noun.

items.analogy_id: Dua gerbong yang digandeng 'and' harus sejenis: music (benda) dan decorations (benda).
items.analogy_en: Two carriages linked by 'and' must match: music (a thing) and decorations (a thing).
items.tip_id: Setelah 'and', cek apakah bentuknya sama dengan bagian sebelum 'and'.
items.tip_en: After 'and', check that the form matches the part before 'and'.

items.prompt: The committee praised her {A}persistent{/A} effort and her {B}creative{/B} approach, which {C}success{/C} {D}solved{/D} the problem.
items.why_correct_id: Langkah 1: dalam clause 'which ___ solved the problem', 'which' adalah subject (pelaku) dan 'solved' adalah verb (kata kerja). Langkah 2: kata di antara subject dan verb yang menerangkan cara menyelesaikan adalah [[adverb]]. 'success' adalah noun; adverb-nya **successfully**.
items.why_correct_en: Step 1: in 'which ___ solved the problem', 'which' is the subject and 'solved' the verb. Step 2: a word between them describing how it solved is an adverb. 'success' is a noun; the adverb is **successfully**.

why_wrong_id.0: 'persistent' adalah adjective yang tepat sebelum 'effort'.
why_wrong_id.1: 'creative' adalah adjective yang tepat sebelum 'approach'.
why_wrong_id.3: 'solved' (V2) adalah verb yang tepat untuk 'which'.

why_wrong_en.0: 'persistent' is a correct adjective before 'effort'.
why_wrong_en.1: 'creative' is a correct adjective before 'approach'.
why_wrong_en.3: 'solved' (V2) is the right verb for 'which'.

items.analogy_id: Di antara sopir (which) dan mesin (solved) hanya ada ruang untuk gaya menyetir, yaitu adverb.
items.analogy_en: Between the driver (which) and the engine (solved) there's only room for driving style: an adverb.
items.tip_id: Subject + ___ + verb → ___ biasanya adverb (-ly). Noun di posisi itu hampir pasti salah.
items.tip_en: Subject + ___ + verb → ___ is usually an adverb (-ly). A noun there is almost always wrong.

items.title: Science at the Bottom of the World
items.body:
Antarctica is the coldest, driest, and windiest continent on Earth, and no one lives there permanently. Yet it is home to dozens of research stations operated by countries from around the world. In winter, only about a thousand people remain on the continent, but in the summer months the population rises to several thousand as scientists arrive to take advantage of the long hours of daylight.

The continent is managed under the Antarctic Treaty, which was signed in 1959 by twelve countries and has since been joined by many more. The treaty sets aside Antarctica for peaceful purposes and for scientific research. Military bases and weapons testing are forbidden, and a later agreement banned mining. Countries may not use their research stations to claim new territory.

Why do scientists accept such difficult conditions? One reason is that Antarctica offers records of the past found nowhere else. By drilling deep into the ice sheet, researchers can remove long cylinders of ice called ice cores. Tiny bubbles trapped in the ice contain samples of ancient air, allowing scientists to measure how the atmosphere has changed over hundreds of thousands of years.

Antarctica is also an excellent place to observe the sky. The air is dry and clean, and there is almost no light pollution, so telescopes can see faint objects clearly. In addition, meteorites that fall onto the ice are easy to spot against the white surface, and many important specimens have been collected there.

Finally, the continent plays an important role in monitoring the health of the planet. It was at an Antarctic station that British scientists first reported, in 1985, a dramatic thinning of the ozone layer, a discovery that led to international action to limit harmful chemicals.

questions.prompt: According to paragraph 2, the Antarctic Treaty forbids all of the following EXCEPT
questions.evidence_quote: The treaty sets aside Antarctica for peaceful purposes and for scientific research.
questions.why_correct_id: Langkah 1: baca paragraf 2 dan centang yang dilarang: pangkalan militer (dilarang), uji senjata (dilarang), klaim wilayah baru (tidak boleh). Langkah 2: penelitian ilmiah justru tujuan perjanjian itu ('for scientific research'). Jadi penelitian ilmiah adalah pengecualiannya.
questions.why_correct_en: Step 1: read paragraph 2 and tick what's forbidden: military bases (forbidden), weapons testing (forbidden), claiming territory (not allowed). Step 2: scientific research is one of the treaty's purposes ('for scientific research'). So research is the exception.

why_wrong_id.0: Pangkalan militer disebut dilarang ('Military bases … are forbidden').
why_wrong_id.1: Uji senjata disebut dilarang.
why_wrong_id.3: Negara tidak boleh memakai stasiun untuk mengklaim wilayah baru.

why_wrong_en.0: Military bases are forbidden.
why_wrong_en.1: Weapons testing is forbidden.
why_wrong_en.3: Stations may not be used to claim new territory.

questions.analogy_id: Soal EXCEPT itu absen kelas: tiga pilihan menjawab 'dilarang', satu pilihan diam karena justru diizinkan.
questions.analogy_en: An EXCEPT question is a roll call: three options answer 'forbidden', one stays silent because it's allowed.
questions.tip_id: Pada soal EXCEPT, jawaban sering justru sesuatu yang DIDUKUNG teks (kebalikan dari kelompoknya).
questions.tip_en: In EXCEPT questions, the answer is often something the text SUPPORTS (the opposite of the group).

questions.prompt: According to the passage, why does the population of Antarctica increase in summer?
options: Tourists arrive to see the ice.
Scientists come to use the long hours of daylight.
Military bases open for the season.
Miners are allowed to work there.
questions.evidence_quote: in the summer months the population rises to several thousand as scientists arrive to take advantage of the long hours of daylight.
questions.why_correct_id: Langkah 1: kata kunci 'summer' ada di akhir paragraf 1. Langkah 2: populasi naik karena ilmuwan datang untuk memanfaatkan siang yang panjang.
questions.why_correct_en: Step 1: 'summer' is at the end of paragraph 1. Step 2: the population rises as scientists arrive to use the long daylight hours.

why_wrong_id.0: Wisatawan tidak disebut.
why_wrong_id.2: Pangkalan militer dilarang oleh perjanjian.
why_wrong_id.3: Pertambangan dilarang oleh perjanjian berikutnya.

why_wrong_en.0: Tourists aren't mentioned.
why_wrong_en.2: Military bases are banned by the treaty.
why_wrong_en.3: Mining is banned by a later agreement.

questions.analogy_id: Kata 'as' di sini berarti 'karena/ketika': ia menghubungkan kenaikan populasi dengan penyebabnya.
questions.analogy_en: 'As' here means 'because/when': it links the population rise to its cause.
questions.tip_id: Soal 'why' tidak selalu memakai 'because'. Kata 'as', 'since', 'so' juga bisa memberi alasan.
questions.tip_en: 'Why' answers don't always use 'because'. 'As', 'since', and 'so' can give reasons too.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is NOT mentioned as a reason Antarctica is a good place to observe the sky?
options: The nights are always free of clouds.
questions.evidence_quote: The air is dry and clean, and there is almost no light pollution, so telescopes can see faint objects clearly.
questions.why_correct_id: Langkah 1: paragraf 4 menyebut alasan: udara kering, udara bersih, hampir tanpa polusi cahaya. Langkah 2: centang ketiganya. Langkah 3: malam yang selalu tanpa awan tidak disebut sama sekali. Itulah jawabannya.
questions.why_correct_en: Step 1: paragraph 4 gives the reasons: dry air, clean air, almost no light pollution. Step 2: tick all three. Step 3: nights always free of clouds is never mentioned, so that's the answer.

why_wrong_id.0: Udara kering disebut ('The air is dry').
why_wrong_id.1: Polusi cahaya yang hampir tidak ada disebut.
why_wrong_id.2: Udara bersih disebut ('and clean').

why_wrong_en.0: Dry air is mentioned.
why_wrong_en.1: Almost no light pollution is mentioned.
why_wrong_en.2: Clean air is mentioned ('and clean').

questions.analogy_id: Pilihan yang terdengar masuk akal (langit malam bersih) tetapi tidak tertulis itu seperti tamu tak diundang: kelihatan cocok, tapi namanya tidak ada di daftar.
questions.analogy_en: A plausible option (cloudless nights) that isn't written is an uninvited guest: it fits in, but its name isn't on the list.
questions.tip_id: Pilihan dengan kata mutlak (always, never) yang tidak ada di teks sering menjadi jawaban soal NOT MENTIONED.
questions.tip_en: Options with absolute words (always, never) not found in the text are often the answer to NOT MENTIONED.

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what do the bubbles in ice cores contain?
questions.evidence_quote: Tiny bubbles trapped in the ice contain samples of ancient air
questions.why_correct_id: Langkah 1: kata kunci 'bubbles' ada di paragraf 3. Langkah 2: gelembung kecil di dalam es berisi sampel udara purba.
questions.why_correct_en: Step 1: 'bubbles' is in paragraph 3. Step 2: the tiny bubbles contain samples of ancient air.

why_wrong_id.1: Meteorit jatuh di permukaan es (paragraf 4), tidak di dalam gelembung.
why_wrong_id.2: Bahan kimia berbahaya disebut terkait lapisan ozon (paragraf 5).
why_wrong_id.3: Air laut beku tidak disebut.

why_wrong_en.1: Meteorites fall on the ice surface (paragraph 4), not inside bubbles.
why_wrong_en.2: Harmful chemicals relate to the ozone layer (paragraph 5).
why_wrong_en.3: Frozen seawater isn't mentioned.

questions.analogy_id: Gelembung di es itu seperti kapsul waktu: menyimpan udara dari ratusan ribu tahun lalu.
questions.analogy_en: Bubbles in ice are time capsules holding air from hundreds of thousands of years ago.
questions.tip_id: Pengecoh soal detail sering diambil dari paragraf lain (meteorit, bahan kimia). Cek paragrafnya.
questions.tip_en: Detail distractors often come from other paragraphs (meteorites, chemicals). Check the paragraph.

questions.prompt: Why does the author mention the thinning of the ozone layer in paragraph 5?
options: To show that Antarctica is getting colder
To give an example of Antarctica's role in monitoring the planet
To argue that mining should be allowed
questions.evidence_quote: Finally, the continent plays an important role in monitoring the health of the planet.
questions.why_correct_id: Langkah 1: kalimat pertama paragraf 5 menyatakan gagasannya: Antarktika berperan memantau kesehatan planet. Langkah 2: penemuan penipisan ozon tahun 1985 adalah contoh nyata peran itu.
questions.why_correct_en: Step 1: paragraph 5's first sentence states its idea: Antarctica helps monitor the planet's health. Step 2: the 1985 ozone discovery is a concrete example of that role.

why_wrong_id.0: Suhu Antarktika yang makin dingin tidak dibahas.
why_wrong_id.2: Teleskop dibahas di paragraf 4.
why_wrong_id.3: Pertambangan dilarang; penulis tidak mendukungnya.

why_wrong_en.0: Antarctica getting colder isn't discussed.
why_wrong_en.2: Telescopes are in paragraph 4.
why_wrong_en.3: Mining is banned; the author doesn't argue for it.

questions.analogy_id: Contoh dalam paragraf itu seperti foto bukti di laporan: menunjukkan bahwa klaim di kalimat pertama benar.
questions.analogy_en: An example in a paragraph is like a photo in a report: proof that the first sentence's claim is true.
questions.tip_id: Soal 'Why does the author mention X?' → cari kalimat pertama paragraf X; X biasanya contohnya.
questions.tip_en: 'Why does the author mention X?' → read the first sentence of X's paragraph; X is usually its example.

items.title: A Drink That Traveled the World
items.body:
Tea is the most widely consumed drink in the world after water, but for most of history it was known only in a small part of Asia. According to Chinese tradition, people in southwestern China were drinking tea thousands of years ago, at first mainly as a medicine.

Over the centuries, tea spread along trade routes. Buddhist monks carried tea seeds from China to Japan, where drinking tea developed into a carefully practiced ceremony. Traders also brought tea across Central Asia and into Russia, where it was often transported by camel caravans.

Tea did not reach Europe as a trade good until the early seventeenth century, when Dutch merchants began shipping it from Asia. At first it was an expensive luxury. In Britain, tea became fashionable after the Portuguese princess Catherine of Braganza, who was already **fond** of the drink, married King Charles II in 1662. Within a century, tea had become a daily habit for people of all classes.

The British demand for tea was so great that the country wanted to stop depending on China for its supply. In the 1830s, British companies began growing tea in the Assam region of India, where a local variety of the plant was found. Later, plantations were established in what is now Sri Lanka and in East Africa, which are still major producers today.

Even the way tea is prepared has changed. According to a popular story, the tea bag was invented by accident in the early 1900s, when a New York merchant sent samples of tea in small silk bags and customers dropped the bags directly into hot water.

questions.prompt: What is the passage mainly about?
options: Why tea is healthier than coffee
The history of the British royal family
How tea spread from China to the rest of the world
How tea bags are made today
questions.evidence_quote: Over the centuries, tea spread along trade routes.
questions.why_correct_id: Langkah 1: paragraf 1 menyebut teh awalnya hanya dikenal di sebagian kecil Asia. Langkah 2: paragraf berikutnya mengikuti penyebarannya: Jepang dan Rusia, Eropa dan Inggris, perkebunan di India dan Afrika, sampai cara penyajiannya. Jadi topiknya penyebaran teh ke seluruh dunia.
questions.why_correct_en: Step 1: paragraph 1 says tea was once known only in a small part of Asia. Step 2: later paragraphs follow its spread: Japan and Russia, Europe and Britain, plantations in India and Africa, and how it's prepared. So the topic is how tea spread worldwide.

why_wrong_id.0: Kopi tidak dibahas.
why_wrong_id.1: Raja Charles II dan Catherine hanya satu contoh di paragraf 3.
why_wrong_id.3: Kantong teh hanya dibahas di paragraf terakhir, dan cara pembuatannya kini tidak dijelaskan.

why_wrong_en.0: Coffee isn't discussed.
why_wrong_en.1: Charles II and Catherine are one example in paragraph 3.
why_wrong_en.3: Tea bags appear only in the last paragraph, and modern manufacturing isn't explained.

questions.analogy_id: Teks sejarah seperti ini itu seperti peta perjalanan: setiap paragraf adalah satu kota yang disinggahi teh.
questions.analogy_en: A history passage like this is a travel map: each paragraph is a city tea passed through.
questions.tip_id: Jika paragraf-paragraf mengikuti urutan waktu atau tempat, ide pokoknya biasanya tentang 'bagaimana X berkembang/menyebar'.
questions.tip_en: If paragraphs follow time or place, the main idea is usually 'how X developed or spread'.

questions.prompt: Which of the following places is NOT mentioned as a place where tea was grown?
questions.evidence_quote: Later, plantations were established in what is now Sri Lanka and in East Africa, which are still major producers today.
questions.why_correct_id: Langkah 1: cari tempat penanaman teh di paragraf 4: India (Assam), Sri Lanka, dan Afrika Timur. Langkah 2: Rusia disebut di paragraf 2 sebagai tujuan perdagangan teh lewat karavan unta, bukan tempat menanamnya.
questions.why_correct_en: Step 1: find where tea was grown in paragraph 4: India (Assam), Sri Lanka, and East Africa. Step 2: Russia appears in paragraph 2 as a destination for traded tea, not a place where it was grown.

why_wrong_id.0: India (wilayah Assam) disebut sebagai tempat perusahaan Inggris mulai menanam teh.
why_wrong_id.1: Sri Lanka disebut sebagai tempat perkebunan.
why_wrong_id.2: Afrika Timur disebut sebagai tempat perkebunan.

why_wrong_en.0: India (Assam) is where British companies began growing tea.
why_wrong_en.1: Sri Lanka is named as a plantation location.
why_wrong_en.2: East Africa is named as a plantation location.

questions.analogy_id: Rusia di teks ini seperti stasiun tujuan kereta barang: teh dikirim ke sana, bukan ditanam di sana.
questions.analogy_en: Russia here is a freight train's destination: tea was shipped there, not grown there.
questions.tip_id: Bedakan peran tempat: asal, tujuan, atau lokasi produksi. Soal NOT sering memanfaatkan perbedaan ini.
questions.tip_en: Separate a place's role: origin, destination, or production. NOT questions often exploit this.

questions.prompt: According to the passage, why did tea become fashionable in Britain?
options: A princess who already liked tea married the king.
Doctors recommended it as a medicine.
It was grown in Britain for the first time.
questions.evidence_quote: In Britain, tea became fashionable after the Portuguese princess Catherine of Braganza, who was already fond of the drink, married King Charles II in 1662.
questions.why_correct_id: Langkah 1: kata kunci 'fashionable' ada di paragraf 3. Langkah 2: teh menjadi tren setelah putri Portugis Catherine, yang sudah menyukai teh, menikah dengan Raja Charles II.
questions.why_correct_en: Step 1: 'fashionable' is in paragraph 3. Step 2: tea became fashionable after Catherine, a Portuguese princess already fond of it, married Charles II.

why_wrong_id.1: Pedagang Belanda membawa teh ke Eropa, tetapi teks tidak menyebut mereka menurunkan harga; teh justru barang mewah.
why_wrong_id.2: Teh sebagai obat disebut untuk Tiongkok kuno (paragraf 1), bukan Inggris.
why_wrong_id.3: Teh tidak ditanam di Inggris; Inggris menanamnya di India.

why_wrong_en.1: Dutch merchants brought tea to Europe, but no price drop is mentioned; it was a luxury.
why_wrong_en.2: Tea as medicine relates to ancient China (paragraph 1), not Britain.
why_wrong_en.3: Tea wasn't grown in Britain; the British grew it in India.

questions.analogy_id: Seperti selebritas yang memakai satu merek tas, lalu semua orang ikut membelinya.
questions.analogy_en: Like a celebrity carrying one brand of bag, and then everyone else buys it too.
questions.tip_id: Kata 'after' bisa menunjukkan sebab dalam soal detail sejarah.
questions.tip_en: 'After' can signal a cause in history detail questions.

questions.prompt: All of the following statements about tea in Europe are true EXCEPT
options: Europeans drank it before the year 1500.
Dutch merchants were the first to ship it there.
It was at first an expensive luxury.
In Britain it became a habit for all classes.
questions.evidence_quote: Tea did not reach Europe as a trade good until the early seventeenth century, when Dutch merchants began shipping it from Asia.
questions.why_correct_id: Langkah 1: centang pernyataan yang benar: pedagang Belanda yang mengirim teh (benar), awalnya barang mewah (benar), di Inggris menjadi kebiasaan semua kalangan (benar). Langkah 2: teks berkata teh baru masuk ke Eropa sebagai barang dagangan pada awal abad ke-17 (1600-an). Jadi 'sebelum tahun 1500' salah.
questions.why_correct_en: Step 1: tick the true statements: Dutch merchants shipped it (true), it was first a luxury (true), it became a habit for all classes in Britain (true). Step 2: the text says tea first reached Europe as a trade good in the early seventeenth century (the 1600s). So 'before 1500' is false.

why_wrong_id.1: Teks: 'when Dutch merchants began shipping it from Asia'.
why_wrong_id.2: Teks: 'At first it was an expensive luxury'.
why_wrong_id.3: Teks: 'tea had become a daily habit for people of all classes'.

why_wrong_en.1: Text: 'when Dutch merchants began shipping it from Asia'.
why_wrong_en.2: Text: 'At first it was an expensive luxury'.
why_wrong_en.3: Text: 'tea had become a daily habit for people of all classes'.

questions.analogy_id: Abad ke-17 itu tahun 1600-an. Mengubah abad menjadi tahun itu seperti mengubah 'jam tujuh malam' menjadi '19.00': artinya sama, angkanya beda.
questions.analogy_en: The seventeenth century is the 1600s. Converting centuries to years is like turning 'seven p.m.' into '19:00': same meaning, different numbers.
questions.tip_id: Ubah 'abad ke-N' menjadi tahun (N-1)00-an agar pilihan berangka tahun mudah dicek.
questions.tip_en: Convert 'Nth century' to the (N-1)00s so year-based options are easy to check.

questions.prompt: The word **fond** in paragraph 3 is closest in meaning to
questions.evidence_quote: who was already fond of the drink
questions.why_correct_id: Langkah 1: kalimatnya menjelaskan mengapa teh menjadi tren setelah pernikahan Catherine: ia sudah 'fond of the drink'. Langkah 2: seseorang yang membuat minuman jadi populer pasti menyukainya. Jadi 'fond' = **keen** (gemar).
questions.why_correct_en: Step 1: the sentence explains why tea became fashionable after Catherine's marriage: she was already 'fond of the drink'. Step 2: someone who makes a drink popular must like it. So 'fond' = **keen**.

why_wrong_id.0: Takut pada teh tidak masuk akal jika ia membuatnya menjadi tren.
why_wrong_id.2: Bosan dengan teh juga bertentangan dengan alasan teh menjadi populer.
why_wrong_id.3: Ia jelas tahu tentang teh karena sudah menyukainya ('already').

why_wrong_en.0: Being afraid of tea doesn't fit someone who made it fashionable.
why_wrong_en.2: Being tired of it contradicts why it became popular.
why_wrong_en.3: She clearly knew about tea, since she 'already' liked it.

questions.analogy_id: Kalau seorang putri membuat minuman jadi tren, ia pasti penggemarnya, bukan orang yang takut atau bosan.
questions.analogy_en: If a princess makes a drink fashionable, she's a fan, not someone afraid of it or tired of it.
questions.tip_id: Cek akibat dalam kalimat (tea became fashionable) untuk menentukan apakah kata itu positif atau negatif.
questions.tip_en: Check the result in the sentence (tea became fashionable) to tell whether the word is positive or negative.
